The IPO:
- Price range: $70 to $78 per share
- 825M shares for sale

The valuation:
- Based on shares outstanding after the IPO: ~$916B to $1.02T
- Fully diluted (including options and unvested stock): ~$1.26T to $1.41T

The numbers (first 9 months of 2026):
- Revenue: $33.2B, ~13x a year ago
- Adjusted operating income: $4.08B (12% margin)
- GAAP operating loss: $1.26B
- Net loss: $104.0B, mostly from a $94.3B non-cash charge on convertible notes due to its valuation increase

- 11,900+ paying $100K+ a year
- 1,900+ paying $1M+ a year
- ~250 paying $10M+ a year
- Revenue per employee: $6.6M, up from $1.4M a year ago

The efficiency:
- Q3 revenue grew 1,127% from a year ago, while compute costs grew 382%
- Anthropic says Opus 5.5 cut customer costs per task by about 40% vs Opus 5

The spending:
- Anthropic has signed $900.9B worth of compute and infrastructure commitments
- $451.6B of that is expected before the end of 2030, and $70.7B is due in the next 12 months

Who controls Anthropic:
- The 7 co-founders hold one special share with 50.1% of the vote
- An independent trust elects a majority of the board
- Public shareholders get 1 vote per share
- Strategic partners like Google and Nvidia get no vote

The lockups:
- Most insiders can't sell for 180 days, and co-founders and large holders for 365 days
- But employees can sell up to 10% of their locked-up shares on the first day of trading
